heroHeadline: DNI Tulsi Gabbard Resigns Citing Husband's Rare Bone Cancer Diagnosis — Last Day Set for June 30
heroSubtitle: Trump on May 23, 2026 (Day 84 of the US-Iran war) declared 'An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization' — claiming Hormuz opening was coming 'shortly.' Within 24 hours, he reversed course on May 24 (Day 85), saying the US was 'in no rush' to finalize. Axios reported exclusively the emerging framework: a 60-day ceasefire + Strait of Hormuz reopening + Iran pledge to never pursue nuclear weapons + enrichment suspension negotiation + Iran's highly-enriched uranium transferred to a third country (possibly Russia) + US ends naval blockade. Iran's semi-official Fars News Agency maintained 'wide disagreements' remained. Brent crude dipped to ~$101/bbl on deal optimism. Separately, USCIS on May 23 issued a sweeping policy memo eliminating routine 'adjustment of status' as a green card pathway — effectively requiring ~500,000 legal H-1B workers, F-1 students, and humanitarian parolees per year to leave the US and apply for green cards through a consulate abroad. The most sweeping legal immigration restriction of Trump's second term, AILA said USCIS is attempting to 'upend decades of processing.' Trump's net approval remains at a second-term low of -20.1.
